diagnostic_evidence.quote: F_{t}(s, \theta) := \vbr{\bigg}{f(s, X_s, \theta), f(s, X_s, \theta) \frac{\Delta W_{t, s}^{\top}}{s - t}}

issues.failure_explanation: The Z-component of F_{t_{n,i}}(t_{n,j},θ) carries the unbounded factor ΔW_{t_{n,i},t_{n,j}}/(t_{n,j}−t_{n,i}). The order-r Taylor remainder in θ is ∂^r f·(R^{n,j})^r·ΔW/(s−t). With R^{n,j}=O(Δt), its conditional expectation is only bounded by CΔt^r·E|ΔW|/(s−t) ~ Δt^{r−1/2}, using s−t ≥ δ_cΔt_n. It is not O(Δt^r) as claimed, and the pre-expectation quantity is not O(·) in the a.s. sense used by the paper. After the factor Δt_n this gives O(Δt^{r+1/2}), not the claimed O(Δt^{r+1}) in eq_expand_dtDF.

failure_location.quote: where the remainder term follows from \eqref{eq_preest_Rni}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the θ-Taylor expansion to order l=r, so the remainder is O(Δt^{r+1})·Δt^{-1/2}. Absorb the extra l=r terms into higher-order trees. State all remainders after conditional expectation, accounting for the half-order loss from ΔW/(s−t).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the claimed O(Δt^{r+1}) local error for the Z-part, and hence consistency order r, is not established by the argument.
issues.title: Taylor remainder in the stage expansion ignores the singular factor ΔW/(s−t)
issues.why_classification: A local extension of the expansion by one order and a careful remainder bound restore the stated rate without new architecture.

then the $Y$ part of \Cref{sch_rk} is convergent with order $r$
the tested Runge-Kutta schemes are still stable and enjoy convergence rates coincident with the theoretical values.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion presents stability and convergence as rigorously proved for the proposed schemes. The paper proves them only under the technical Assumption assu_FLipVar, which is verified only for z-independent Lipschitz f (and then only for the Y-part) or for linear f. Both numerical examples use generators nonlinear in z, for which only numerical evidence is offered. Stability is not derived from the Butcher-tree theory at all.

failure_location.quote: Based on this theory, we also rigorously prove the stability, and convergence of the proposed schemes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claim: stability/convergence are proved under Assumption assu_FLipVar, which covers z-independent f (Y-part only) or linear f; the general nonlinear case is supported only numerically.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are misled about the scope of the convergence guarantee, especially for nonlinear z-dependent generators.
issues.title: Conclusion overclaims a rigorous stability/convergence proof for the proposed schemes
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws the advertised general convergence guarantee, a substantive loss of claimed scope, though no proof changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Passing from eq_estEtniDelFtnij to eq_estDelFtnij uses E ρ²(E_{t_{n,j}}X − E_{t_{n,i}}X) ≤ E ρ²(X) − E ρ²(E_{t_n}X). This is a Pythagorean identity for conditional expectations, which holds when ρ² is a positive semidefinite quadratic form. It fails for general seminorms, yet Assumption assu_FLipVar and the lemma allow an arbitrary seminorm ρ.
